title: PLG Signals → Packaging & Pricing Guidance (Hosted → Dedicated → Private)
author: Isabelle Laurent
body:
## Purpose
This page provides **consistent guidance** for AEs/SDRs/SEs on how to translate high-signal PLG triggers into:
- a recommended **packaging motion** (Hosted → Dedicated; Dedicated → Private)
- a **commercial ask** (commit, term, discount parameters)
- guardrails for **free-credit / proof-of-value** exceptions

This is intended to reduce false-positive “sales motions,” prevent inconsistent discounting, and ensure we offer the right deployment mode for the customer’s constraints.

## Scope
Applies to:
- **Self-serve Hosted API** accounts routed via PLG signals (new logos and expansions)
- **Dedicated** customers showing Private intent (residency, compliance, on-prem)

Out of scope:
- Renewal pricing policy (handled in the Renewals playbook)
- Custom enterprise legal/security terms (handled by Legal + Security review)

## Packaging definitions (quick refresher)
**Hosted API**
- Multi-tenant hosted endpoints
- Usage-based billing, fastest time-to-value

**Dedicated**
- Reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and data isolation
- SLA-backed uptime/latency targets
- Best for: sustained throughput, concurrency spikes, rate-limit friction, predictable unit economics

**Private (VPC / on-prem)**
- Customer-controlled networking + private control plane
- Best for: strict security/compliance, data residency, audit controls, regulated workloads, network isolation

## Principles (how to decide)
1) **Sell the constraint, not the SKU.** Start from the pain (latency, rate limits, isolation, residency, auditability).
2) **Propose the smallest step that removes risk.** Hosted → Dedicated first unless residency/security/networking requires Private.
3) **Commits follow predictability.** Don’t push annuals before we can size capacity and prove baseline throughput.
4) **Discounts are for term & certainty.** Reward prepay and longer commitments; avoid discounting to compensate for missing product fit.
5) **Credits are for evaluation only.** Credits are not a substitute for a commercial agreement or for ongoing production.

---

## Signal → Motion decision matrix
Use this table for the “default” recommendation. Deviations require manager approval (see Deal Desk section).

| Primary signal (from PLG pipeline) | Typical customer statement / symptom | Recommended motion | Default offer | What we ask for first | Notes / qualification questions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sustained spend growth (30d) | “This is in production; usage is climbing.” | Hosted → Dedicated (commercial discovery) | Dedicated reserved capacity (regional) | Monthly commit sized to last 30d usage + headroom | Confirm traffic pattern (peaks), target p95 latency, and model mix. |
| Concurrency spikes / bursty load | “We get slammed during business hours.” | Hosted → Dedicated (PoC) | Dedicated with autoscaling policy + burst option | 4–6 week PoC → convert to 12-month term | Dedicated often reduces tail latency + rate limiting. |
| Repeated 429/rate-limit hits | “We keep hitting limits; can you raise them?” | Hosted → Dedicated (fast-track) | Dedicated + tuned quotas | Paid PoC or immediate commit if urgent | If they only need higher limits temporarily, confirm seasonality before locking capacity. |
| Repeated latency complaints / routing failures | “Latency is inconsistent; errors during peak.” | Hosted → Dedicated (SE-led) | Dedicated + performance tuning (batching/caching) | PoC with success criteria (SLOs) | If issue is app-side (timeouts, retry storms), fix first; avoid selling Dedicated as a band-aid. |
| Security intent (SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2, DPA) | “Procurement requires SSO/audit logs/SOC2.” | Hosted → Dedicated OR Private (depending on requirement) | Dedicated + security package; Private if network isolation/residency required | Security review kickoff + timeline | If they require VPC-only, customer-managed egress controls, or on-prem: go Private. |
| Data residency / regional pinning | “Must keep data in EU / specific region.” | Hosted → Dedicated in-region OR Private VPC | Dedicated (eu-west) when available; otherwise Private | Confirm region requirement + sub-processors | EMEA: validate if “EU-only processing” is mandatory vs “EU preferred.” |
| “Contact sales” + pricing page repeat visits | “We’re evaluating vendors / comparing options.” | SDR qualification → AE discovery | Usually Dedicated for scaling workloads | Meeting + mutual action plan | Treat as intent, not proof of need—confirm usage + constraints. |
| Private docs engagement (VPC/on-prem) | “Need VPC / private networking / air-gapped.” | Dedicated → Private (or Hosted → Private if required) | Private platform fee + support tier | Architecture review + security questionnaire | Private motions require earlier SE involvement. |

---

## Default thresholds (when to propose packaging)
These are **starting points** for consistent outreach and offer framing. Thresholds are evaluated over rolling windows (7/14/30d) and deduped per signal policy.

### Hosted → Dedicated (default)
Propose Dedicated when **any** of the following are true and the customer confirms production intent:
- **Sustained spend:** ≥ **$7,500 in the last 30 days** OR ≥ **$2,500 in the last 7 days** (excluding one-time test spikes)
- **Concurrency pressure:** p95 concurrent requests ≥ **25** for ≥ **3 days** in last 14 days (or clear peak-hour saturation)
- **Rate-limit friction:** ≥ **3 distinct days** with rate-limit events (429s) above account baseline AND customer requested limit increases/support
- **Reliability pain:** repeated model-routing failures or elevated error rate impacting production (validate against incident/support notes)

Fast-track Dedicated (skip long PoC) when:
- customer has a defined launch date ≤ **21 days**, AND
- they accept a minimum term/commit (see “Commit sizing”)

### Dedicated → Private (default)
Propose Private when **any** of the following are true:
- **Network isolation requirement:** VPC-only access, private connectivity, customer-controlled routing/egress policies
- **Regulated environment:** on-prem / air-gapped requirement
- **Compliance/residency:** contractual requirement for data processing restrictions that Dedicated cannot satisfy (e.g., specific country residency, customer-managed KMS/HSM, restricted audit visibility requirements)

Note: “Security intent” alone does not always mean Private. Many security checklists can be satisfied in Dedicated with the right evidence package and controls.

---

## Commit sizing & commercial asks
### Dedicated: recommended commit anchors
Use anchors to create consistency; final sizing should be validated by SE capacity estimate.

**Minimum entry commit (Dedicated):**
- Default: **$12k/month** (or local currency equivalent)
- Typical term: **12 months**

**Mid-market / growth commit:**
- **$25k–$60k/month** depending on concurrency and model mix

**Large / spiky workloads:**
- **$75k+/month** or multi-pool designs (regional HA)

**How to size quickly (rule of thumb):**
- Start with last 30d spend, remove obvious spikes, then add **15–30% headroom** if they have peak-hour patterns.

### Private: pricing structure (high-level)
Private is typically sold as:
- **Platform fee** (covers control plane + private deployment packaging)
- **Support tier** (standard vs premium)
- **Capacity costs** (hardware/infra costs depending on environment)

Private deals should be positioned around risk reduction (residency, auditability, network isolation) rather than pure unit economics.

---

## Discount guidance (guardrails)
Discounting must be consistent and tied to customer value and deal certainty.

### Standard discount levers (allowed without Deal Desk escalation)
- **Annual prepay:** up to **10%**
- **Multi-year (24 months):** up to **15%** (requires Sales leadership approval in-region)
- **Volume/scale step function:** acceptable when tied to committed ramp (document ramp schedule)

### What we avoid
- Discounting solely to “match” a competitor without validated scope equivalence
- Discounts to compensate for missing technical requirements (route to SE/product gap assessment instead)
- “Stacking” discounts with large free credits (see below)

### Escalation required
Escalate to Deal Desk (Sales Ops + CRO approval) if any of the following are true:
- Discount > **15%**
- Any non-standard payment terms (net-60+, custom milestones)
- Customer requests unlimited usage or uncapped burst without pricing protections
- Contract contains non-standard liability/indemnity or residency obligations

---

## Free-credit / proof-of-value exceptions (strict guardrails)
Credits can be useful for evaluation, but they create long-term pricing confusion if not controlled.

### Allowed uses (default)
Credits may be offered only when all are true:
- Customer has an active evaluation with a documented **mutual action plan** (MAP)
- Credits are time-bound and tied to a clear success criterion (latency/throughput/SLO)
- The customer agrees to a follow-up milestone and commercial next step

### Not allowed uses
- Ongoing “production subsidy” for an already live Hosted workload
- Credits as a substitute for capacity reservation on Dedicated
- Credits to overcome procurement delays without a signed agreement

### Credit caps (without CRO approval)
- **Hosted evaluation:** up to **$1,500** one-time, expires in **30 days**
- **Dedicated PoC:** prefer discounted PoC fee over credits; if credits are required, cap at **$5,000** equivalent and expire in **45 days**

### Required approvals
- Any credits: AE manager + Sales Ops (Isabelle Laurent) approval in Slack/Deal Desk channel
- ≥ $5,000 equivalent credits or any credit stacking with discounting: CRO (Jordan Blake)
- Private-related credits (platform fee waivers): CRO + Legal (Michael Grant) + SE lead (Markus Klein)

### Required language (include in email / order form notes)
- “Credits are for evaluation use only and expire on <date>. Unused credits do not roll over and are not valid for production SLAs.”

---

## Recommended talk tracks by motion
### Hosted → Dedicated (unit economics + reliability)
- “Dedicated removes multi-tenant contention and rate limiting, and gives you predictable throughput so you can hit your p95 latency targets.”
- “We can tune batching/caching for your traffic pattern; Dedicated makes those optimizations more reliable.”

### Dedicated → Private (risk + compliance)
- “Private is the right fit when your security/residency requirements need network isolation or customer-controlled environments.”
- “We’ll align the deployment architecture to your compliance timeline and evidence needs (audit logs, key management, access controls).”

---

## Examples (how to apply the guidance)
1) **Account with $9k in 30d spend + repeated 429s**
- Motion: Hosted → Dedicated
- Ask: $12k/mo, 12 months; fast-track if launch date is near
- Guardrail: do not offer large credits; propose 4-week PoC only if sizing uncertain

2) **EU-based customer scaling embeddings + region requirement (EU-only)**
- Motion: Hosted → Dedicated in eu-west (if available)
- Ask: commit sized to steady-state; confirm whether “EU-only processing” is contractual
- If strict country-level residency required: escalate to Private assessment

3) **Dedicated customer requesting VPC-only and customer-managed key controls**
- Motion: Dedicated → Private
- Ask: architecture review + security questionnaire; align to procurement timeline
- Commercial: platform fee + support tier; avoid heavy discounting before scope is finalized

---

## Operational checklist (for AEs/SDRs)
Before proposing pricing/packaging, confirm:
1) Current deployment mode and whether they are production
2) Which pain is primary: cost, latency, rate limits, security, residency
3) Traffic pattern (peaks, concurrency) and model mix
4) Required regions and timeline constraints
5) Whether there is an existing opp/CSM-managed account (suppression rules)

Then:
- Log packaging recommendation + rationale in HubSpot notes
- Attach MAP if offering PoC or credits
- Route to SE early for Dedicated sizing or any Private discussion

## FAQ
**Q: Customer asks for Dedicated “just to lower cost.” Should we do it?**
A: Only if their traffic is steady enough to benefit from reserved capacity and we can size appropriately. Otherwise focus on Hosted optimization (batching/caching guidance) first.

**Q: When is it okay to offer a discounted PoC instead of credits?**
A: Prefer a paid PoC when capacity and SE time are material. Use a time-boxed PoC fee that can convert into the first month of commit upon signature.

**Q: A customer wants Private because it “sounds more secure.”**
A: Validate the requirement. If Dedicated satisfies the checklist (SSO/audit logs/SOC2 evidence) and residency isn’t strict, keep them on Dedicated to reduce complexity.
